lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: You're listening to Smoke Ring Trio. A little jazz club, inside a storm cloud. Mind the step. There isn't one.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Smoke Ring Trio. Piano, bass and brushes, about two miles up. Find a table, darling. Hold on to it.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: This is Smoke Ring Trio. If you feel the floor give a little, that's only the cloud. It's listening too.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Smoke Ring Trio. It's late. The candles are low, the cloud is high, and nobody in here is in any hurry at all.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Smoke Ring Trio, eighty eight point eight five. No smoking, please. The room does quite enough of that on its own.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: You're in the Cumulus Room, home of the Smoke Ring Trio. Tonight's forecast: brushes, with a chance of piano.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Smoke Ring Trio. The cloud has drifted somewhere sunny this afternoon. We've drawn the curtains. It's night in here. It always is.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: That piano solo was a warm front. It came in low from the west, it lingered over the middle eight, and it left everybody slightly damp around the eyes.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The bass is now clearing from the north. Lovely conditions. Stay exactly where you are.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: A reminder for those of you in the room. Please don't applaud. We're inside a cloud, and every time you clap, it rains on somebody down below.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Last week's standing ovation fell on a village fête. They carried on. They always carry on. So in here we snap our fingers. Snapping is drizzle. Drizzle is fine.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Florian, our waiter, is crossing to table nine with a tray of drinks. He set off at the start of the last number.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: You have to go carefully, crossing a cloud. You have to believe in every single step. He's halfway. He's doing beautifully. Let's give him one more ballad.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: News from the floor. Florian has reached table nine. Table nine had drifted off towards the bandstand during the ballad, but he followed it with great dignity, and he didn't spill a drop.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The ice has melted. They're delighted. Florian?

lines.speaker: Florian, the Waiter
lines.text: Very good, madam. Setting off for table ten.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: A word about Silas, our drummer. Silas plays with brushes, and he plays them so softly that some nights he's only a rumour.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: People ask me, is there really a drummer? There is, darling. Look closely. That faint weather at the back of the stage. That's Silas.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Augustin, on the bass, has been walking the same bass line since the spring. It's a long walk. He doesn't hurry it.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Tonight, for the first time, I think he can see home. Listen for it. Somewhere in the next tune, the bass is going to arrive.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Did you hear it, at the end of that one? The bass got home. Months on the road, and Augustin walked it right up to the front door.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: And then he turned round, and started walking back. Of course he did. He's a bass player. Here's the walk back.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Tonight's forecast in the room. Scattered piano, mostly in the upper register. A low bank of bass settling over the front tables. Brushes, light and variable.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: And a ninety percent chance of the pianist closing her eyes, and not opening them again until the bridge.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Bev's in again, at the bar, still looking for her song. Tonight she hummed it to Mercy, at the piano. Da da dum. Da da.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Mercy played it straight back to her, with three new chords in it. Bev cried. Bev says it still isn't the song. But it's closer. Keep looking, darling.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: A word for the operator on the relay ship, drifting slowly under the cloud. We can see your running lights through the floor.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: There's a table by the window, darling, if you ever come up. We'll keep the candle going. This one's for the night shift.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: If you saw a flicker in the walls just then, that was the lightning. It lives in here with us. It's terribly shy. It only comes out for the ballads.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: We've asked it to sit in for a number. It says it can't read music. It just knows when.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Tonight's set comes to you courtesy of Grumbel's Ladders. Getting up to a club inside a cloud takes a very long ladder, and a very calm disposition.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. Down is a long way, darling, so take your time.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Good evening. The cloud is drifting west tonight, over the hills and the lit-up farms.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: If you're down there, and you hear a piano in the rain, wave. We'll see you. We won't wave back. We'll be playing.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to the Supper Club Forecast. The tables are floating, the candles are lit, and the soup is, as ever, mostly cloud.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: A note from the kitchen. Tonight the chef recommends the consommé. It's a clear soup, which, up here, makes it the only clear thing in the building.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The trio will now play something to digest to.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Table six has ordered the chocolate cake for two. It's arrived. It's floating. They're chasing it gently with their spoons.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: That's romance, darling. Here's something for the chase.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: It's three in the morning, and this is the Three AM Set. The diners have gone. The trio is playing for each other now. Pull up a cloud. Keep your voice down.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: This is the hour when Mercy plays the tune she wrote for someone who never came to hear it. She doesn't say who.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: She plays it every night, at about this time, just in case. Here it is. Or something very like it.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: At this time of night the cloud goes very still, and the lightning in the walls is only resting. You can hear Augustin's fingers on the strings. You can hear the candles.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: You can hear yourself, too. Don't worry. You sound lovely.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Good morning. This is the Morning After, on Smoke Ring Trio. The chairs are on the tables, the coffee's on, and the trio is playing. Nobody's had the heart to tell them.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The cleaner has come in. She's mopping the cloud. It doesn't need mopping, it's a cloud, but she says it's the principle.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The trio is playing her a waltz. She is pretending very hard not to dance.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Silas has fallen asleep at the drums. He's still playing. Some of his finest brushwork, honestly. I wouldn't dream of waking him.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: We have a guest tonight. We're a trio. We've always been a trio. But there's a cold draught by the piano, and it has been keeping perfect time since Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: It won't say who it is. It likes the minor keys. So tonight, darlings, we're a quartet.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Smoke Ring Trio. The cloud has gone dark grey for Halloween. It's been practising.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The cloud drifted past the place where a moon used to be, darlings. Everyone says one's missing. Nobody can agree which.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Mercy played a little something into the gap. It sounded like a moon. Close enough.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The whole room smells of toast. So, they tell me, does everywhere else.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Florian swears it isn't the kitchen. We haven't got a kitchen. We have a small cloud with a kettle on it.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: There's a tune going round, darlings, the whole dial's humming it, and nobody can finish it.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Mercy's been playing the first half all night. She's waiting for somebody else to play the end. That's jazz.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Three knocks at the stage door. Silas played them back on the snare, very softly.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: There was nobody there. There never is, in a cloud. But it was a lovely rhythm.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: The sky outside the Cumulus Room went a colour just now. There's no word for it.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Augustin stopped walking his bass line, for the first time since spring. Then he picked it up again, a little slower.

lines.speaker: Florian, the Waiter
lines.text: Madame Octavia, there is a pigeon at table nine.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Is it ordering, Florian?

lines.speaker: Florian, the Waiter
lines.text: It asked for the usual.

lines.speaker: Octavia Lowe
lines.text: Then bring it the usual, darling. It's clearly been here before.
